what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three of the four previous focus items were drawn, worked and landed -- `13ecd0186` scoped the switching curve to its evidence, `703269e51` landed the widened world's three-arm reading, `7af34caa0` widened the discoverability scan from three axes to five -- and the fourth, EP1, was drawn and not repaired. Correcting the brief once more: it reports `drawn: [EP1]`, the one item that did NOT land, and is blind to the three kebab-slug items that did. So the loop my three predecessors left open is now closed: the instrument exists, it was pointed at the widened world, and it produced a reading with an error bar. Here is what it says, and it is the most important paragraph this project has written. On the widened S1 world the control (flat rules) nets GBP 113,282.62, the per-customer value arm GBP 120,648.84, and the level arm -- the same flat rule charging the value arm's own realised median of GBP 44.50/MWh -- GBP 120,823.40. The selection leg is therefore MINUS GBP 174.57 and the level explains 102.4% of the advantage. Against four seeds on the narrower world the selection leg has a standard deviation of GBP 3,121.20 about a mean of MINUS GBP 165.83, so the point estimate is roughly a twentieth of the band it sits in: the per-customer advantage is not distinguishable from zero, and never has been. The mechanism is now visible and it is not flattering. The value arm's win is that it shed 433,602 kWh (5.4% of volume) whose gross margin per kWh ran below its own network and policy cost per kWh; 87.3% of the gross-margin difference sits on FIVE differentially-churned accounts, and 6 of its 25 priced decisions were set by the lawful price cap rather than by anything about the customer, on one account carrying 43% of the money that moved. The level arm gets the same money by charging everyone more and letting the same marginal volume go. Read against the director's thesis, the honest statement is: a BASELINE now exists, it is winning, and the advantage that does exist comes from a LEVEL move any supplier could make without knowing anything about a customer. That is not backwards -- it is the first real answer -- but the experiment cannot currently support a stronger claim in either direction, because it contains 25 renewal decisions across a decade on a book of 210 settled accounts, and because the artefact publishes two irreconcilable net margins for the same arm, GBP 39,962.17 apart. Every item below exists to make the next reading say something a reader can rely on.

focus.what: `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_s1_three_arm.json` publishes two net margins for the SAME control arm on the SAME run and they differ by GBP 39,962.17. Observed: `control_arm.total_net_gbp` = 113,282.617135 with `total_bad_debt_gbp` = 46,428.5849 and `final_treasury_gbp` = 363,282.617; `gross_to_net_bridge.control_arm.net_margin_gbp` = 153,244.792 with `bad_debt_gbp` = 6,466.41 and `unexplained_residual_gbp` of 8e-4. The difference between the two net figures equals the difference between the two bad-debt sums to the penny. `simulation/run_phase2b.py:2502` computes `total_net` as the sum of `net_margin_gbp` over `all_records`, which is the 153,244.79 basis and is the GBP 153,245 the site and every auto-process commit message publishes. Inferred, not yet observed: `final_treasury_gbp` = 250,000 + `total_net_gbp` exactly, so the arm block reads a treasury-derived (banked) figure. Whatever the cause, `level_vs_selection.basis` currently reads "settled net margin (R14) -- `net_margin_gbp` from the world's own settled records" while the numbers it sums are the 113k block, so at least one label is false and R14 is breached inside the artefact that carries the thesis. Do three things. FIRST, name each figure's true clock -- settled, billed or banked -- from the code that produces it, and fix the labels rather than the numbers. SECOND, decide which basis the arms are scored on and say why in the module; this is not cosmetic, because on the arm-block basis the value arm avoids GBP 2,481 of bad debt and on the records basis it incurs GBP 216 MORE, so the two bases disagree on the SIGN of bad debt's contribution to the headline advantage. THIRD, make it impossible to reintroduce: a control that fails when the artefact publishes two net margins for one arm without a declared clock on each, R15-proven by mutating one label. Then re-derive `level_vs_selection` on the declared basis and say in the artefact whether MINUS GBP 174.57 moved.
focus.why: Everything downstream is a number read off this file, including the only comparison the thesis has, and one of the two figures it publishes for the same arm is mislabelled. It goes first because it is cheap -- two call sites and a docstring -- and because it is the one defect here that could make a published figure wrong rather than merely imprecise: a reader who sees GBP 153,245 on the site and GBP 113,283 in the experiment has no way to know both describe the same run. Finished when each net figure in the artefact carries its own clock traced to the code that produced it, the arms' basis is declared with a stated reason, the sign of bad debt's contribution is settled, and a control fires on an unclocked pair. If the two figures turn out to be a legitimate settled-versus-banked pair -- which is the likeliest answer -- that is a complete result and the repair is the label and the control, not the arithmetic. R12 applies without qualification: do not let the choice of basis be made by which one flatters the arm.

focus.what: The experiment that grades per-customer decision-making contains 25 decisions. Observed in the same artefact: `decision_shape.priced` = 25 with `declined` = 0 for the value arm, and `level_arm_decision_shape.priced` = 34 -- a 36% larger denominator for an arm that is supposed to differ from the value arm in `renewal_margin_arm` and nothing else, over a book of 210 billing accounts settled in the window and 127 alive at its end. Renewals are annual: `churn_model._renewal_periods` derives them from acquisition_date + 365n, and `company/pricing/renewal_rate_chain.py` records that an earlier ten-year A/B saw 66. Build the funnel and publish it as a first-class block in the artefact: how many renewal events the world generates across the window, how many reach `decide_renewal_rate` (`simulation/run_phase2b.py:1344`), how many reach `renewal_margin_uplift` with an arm set, and how many are priced versus declined -- with the drop at each stage named. Then answer the two questions it raises. (a) Is the small population a WORLD property -- most of the book on evergreen or variable tariffs that never present a renewal decision -- or a gate in the chain? If it is the world, that is a finding about how much of the book per-customer pricing can touch at all, and it must be written down in those words rather than fixed. (b) Why do two arms differing only in `renewal_margin_arm` see different numbers of renewals? The likely answer is that divergent churn moves the roster and therefore the renewal schedule, which is legitimate sequential-A/B behaviour -- but it is currently unstated, and `arm_identity` guards the POLICY fields while nothing guards the decision POPULATION. State the mechanism with evidence and add the count difference to the artefact beside the advantage, so no reader takes a per-decision claim from two different denominators.
focus.why: This is the reason the headline cannot be resolved, and it is upstream of every proposal to widen the world further. A selection effect worth a few hundred pounds spread across 25 decisions, five of which carry 87% of the money and six of which were priced by the price cap, cannot be separated from noise by any amount of re-running -- at the observed seed spread it would take on the order of forty full decade runs to resolve a GBP 1,400 effect, which is the honest arithmetic and the reason to change the experiment rather than repeat it. Second rather than first only because item one may change the numbers it reports. Finished when the artefact carries the funnel with the drop named at each stage, the arms' differing denominators have a stated and evidenced mechanism, and there is a written answer to whether the decision surface is small by construction or by plumbing. If it is small by construction, say so plainly and stop -- do not raise the count by relaxing something in the world to make the experiment easier, which would be R13 straight through the wall. R12: the funnel is a diagnostic.

focus.what: Carried forward unchanged and unrepaired: the atom was drawn this stretch and `tools/couple_clv.py:606` still defines `_earliest_belief`, and `docs/observability/coupled_gap_ledger.json` still records "The belief taken is the EARLIEST year-end snapshot". Fix the coupler's belief-selection rule so EP1 grades a belief capable of varying. The diagnosis is landed and correct (`4b6e1b29f`, `docs/observability/EP1_GRADED_SLICE_WHAT_IT_IS_EVIDENCE_FOR_2026-08-27.md`): the earliest year-end snapshot is exactly the point where `churn_probability = BASE + 0 x UPLIFT` (`saas/churn_model.py:39`, `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py:580`) because no bill-shock history has accrued, so the hazard is 0.05 for 154 of 154 accounts by construction and `distinct_hazards: 1` measures the rule, not the company. The stated justification -- that a ceased account has no other snapshot -- is false for 14 of the 20 graded accounts still present. Replace it with a rule that grades a belief the company actually held while the account was live, write the new rule AND its reason into the module docstring beside the one it replaces, and keep the existing fallback for accounts that genuinely have one snapshot. R15 both ways: the mutation that must go red is reverting to the earliest snapshot with an assertion that `distinct_hazards` stays above one; and the new rule must not pass by reading a field the belief producer also writes -- trace the FIELD, per this project's own lesson that a cross-layer import is not automatically a tautology. Then run `python3 -m tools.couple_clv` and land the row. The headline `gap = 2.529` stays unpublished until the row is honest.
focus.why: This is the company half of the thesis -- whether the supplier's per-customer lifetime-value belief is worth anything -- and it is the only instrument that grades it. The atom's own map entry says "EP1 has not been graded ONCE" at level 2 against a target of 3, so it is also the only level move currently available on evidence. It is third and not last on purpose: it has been named on six lists and reached on two, it is independent of the A/B artefact and of the tree lock so it can proceed alongside items one and two, and its two owed halves are now fully diagnosed with nothing left to think about. Finished when the ledger row is measured under the new rule and states how many distinct hazards the graded population contains. If that is more than one and the coupled rung is met, self-certify the level with `record_level_up_self_certified` -- and never `--no-verify` a `level_current` change. R12: the gap is a diagnostic. A belief that turns out badly calibrated once it can vary is a finding, not a defect in the fix.

focus.what: The single most important thing this project has established reaches no reader. Observed: `grep -rl "level_share_of_advantage|value_cycle_ab|selection_gbp"` across `site/`, `tools/generate_dashboard_data.py`, `saas/reporting/` and `docs/reports/` returns one file, `site/data/delivery.json`, which carries a lane claim and not a figure. The site and the annual report publish a profitable supplier at GBP 153,245 net and say nothing about the flat-rules baseline that matches it. Put the comparison in front of a reader on a business surface: the three arms with their net margins, the selection leg, the seed spread beside it, the number of decisions it rests on, and the clock from item one. Label the reading PROVISIONAL, which keeps it retractable and therefore squarely inside this seat's authority. Write the finding in the same voice the artefact already uses -- that a selection worth nothing is a complete answer and not a cue to tune the arm. Then verify to the rendered value per R11: fetch the LIVE deployed surface and quote the actual rendered figure, not the data file, not origin, not the deploy log; assert both the data stamp and the visible number. Update `docs/staging/done/WORKER_FINDING_THE_VALUE_ARMS_ADVANTAGE_IS_THE_LEVEL_NOT_THE_SELECTION_2026-08-27.md` to match what is published, and archive `docs/staging/in_progress/LANE0_THREE_ARM_AB_ON_THE_S1_WORLD_2026-08-27.md`, whose block is now dead.
focus.why: The director's thesis contains the requirement in terms: "there has to be a BASELINE to beat -- the same book run by a supplier applying flat rules with no per-customer view -- or 'it performed well' means nothing." We built that baseline, it is currently beating the per-customer arm, and a reader of our own published surfaces cannot tell. Publishing a profitable-looking supplier while withholding the comparison that qualifies it is the closest thing to a misleading claim on this project, and the remedy is ours to take, not his: PROVISIONAL figures are explicitly retractable and therefore not one of the four reserved classes. Last of the four because items one and two determine what the number and its caveat should say. Finished when the live surface renders the three arms, the selection leg, its seed spread and its decision count, and the fetched evidence is quoted. It must NOT wait for a better number: publish the current reading with its error bar. A negative result about our own arm, published honestly, is worth more to this thesis than a positive one we cannot resolve.

entries.what: The A/B artefact publishes two net margins for the same control arm, GBP 39,962.17 apart, and the block the thesis is read off carries a false basis label. Observed: `control_arm.total_net_gbp` = 113,282.617135 with `total_bad_debt_gbp` = 46,428.5849, against `gross_to_net_bridge.control_arm.net_margin_gbp` = 153,244.792 with `bad_debt_gbp` = 6,466.41, the two differences equal to the penny; and `level_vs_selection.basis` reads "settled net margin (R14) -- `net_margin_gbp` from the world's own settled records" while summing the first block. The consequence is not academic -- on one basis the value arm avoids GBP 2,481 of bad debt and on the other it incurs GBP 216 more, so the two disagree on the sign of bad debt's contribution to the advantage. Item one is the repair.

EP1 was drawn and not repaired for the third consecutive stretch in which it was named. `tools/couple_clv.py:606` still defines `_earliest_belief`, `git log` on that file shows no commit this stretch, and `docs/observability/coupled_gap_ledger.json` still carries "The belief taken is the EARLIEST year-end snapshot". The previously published selection figure of MINUS GBP 1,388.80 was reported as a quantity and is not one. Four seeds put its standard deviation at GBP 3,121.20 about a mean of MINUS GBP 165.83 -- 0.11 standard errors from zero -- and the underlying noise-floor harness had been patched onto `price_sensitivity_for_customer`, a symbol the churn decision stopped calling when it moved to `price_elasticity_for_customer`, so every seed had been running a byte-identical world and would have reported a noise floor of exactly zero. The widened world's reading and the two reds that had refused its land were both closed this stretch after failing twice in one afternoon. `8d8e9c2c8` established that both reds were pre-existing at clean HEAD -- the check my predecessor asked for, run against a clean checkout rather than the dirty tree -- and that the treasury null control was correct rather than broken, so no gate exclusion was reached for. `703269e51` landed the reading. Observed, `docs/observability/three_arm_composite_run.log`: unit `land-then-three-arm-ab.service` launched 19:45:12Z, `2 failed, 485 passed in 621.40s`, `[land] rc=1 2026-08-27T19:55:59Z`, `END rc=1 PHASE=land -- gate refused, A/B deliberately NOT run`; `systemctl --user is-active` reads `failed`; `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_s1_three_arm.json` does not exist. The discoverability control landed covering three of the five axes that carry the claim, and its own whole-set guard cannot see the gap. Observed: `tests/simulation/test_discoverability_claims_are_enforced.py::_axes()` filters `key.endswith("_marginals")`; `docs/design/segmentation_curriculum_v1.json` carries `hidden_truth_only` on five keys, and the two the filter drops -- `tenure_adoption_gating_strength` and `region_marginal_synthetic_acquisitions` -- both declare `false`, i.e. both claim discoverable, and neither has a probe. `MIN_AXES_SCANNED = 3` is pinned to what the filter returns, so the control written to catch a missed axis is satisfied by its own blindness. This is the catalogued shape where an exclusion scoped by a naming convention hides everything that convention mixes, and the previous focus item asked in terms for a control that "must enumerate EVERY axis the curriculum declares".

The steer-effectiveness signal reported `drawn: []` for the fifth consecutive stretch while all four focus items were drawn, worked and landed (`3cefa754b`, `9e52d2254`, `4b6e1b29f`, `e0cce68d1`). Recorded here again because a seat that took the brief at face value would conclude its own lever had failed and redesign a mechanism that is working. By R3's two-strike rule this is three strikes past the line for repair; see `not_now` for why I am still declining and what would change that.

The `oom_kills_total` counter was cited in the previous direction as evidence that the 15:08Z run died of memory pressure. It is not a memory-pressure signal: all 64 `Killed process` records in a `dmesg` buffer covering the whole window carry `oom_memcg=.../ops2-peak-kill-selftest-<pid>.scope`, a cgroup created by this repository's own `tests/tools/test_measure_publish_gate_subject_cost.py`, and none falls in the run's window at all. The run was reaped as a bounded tick's descendant, which reparenting fixed. Found, measured and written up this stretch.

The third and final reading of EP1's constant hazard, correcting two previous directions including mine. Direction one blamed the estimator; direction two blamed the outcome-selected graded slice. Both are refuted by measurement: 100 of 101 multi-snapshot accounts move off their first hazard, and at each account's EARLIEST snapshot the hazard is 0.05 for 154 of 154 -- the whole book, not a selected 33. The cause is the coupler's own belief-selection rule. Landed as `4b6e1b29f` with the consequences taken: the `gap = 2.529` is not published in its current form, the re-run was not run because it could not have changed the answer, and no level move was available. Item three is the repair.

The noise-floor measurement now in flight patches a function the churn decision no longer calls, so it cannot see the thing it exists to measure.
